text:
How might we be able to teach a machine to tell the difference between an earthquake signal and all the other shaking recorded by a seismometer?

A seismometer records shaking in the ground all day, every day. Some of that shaking comes from earthquakes—but much of it doesn't. We saw in the first activity the jumping up and down makes seismic waves.

On the right you will see two different signals. One is a signal of people jumping and one is a signal of an earthquake. Look closely at the images. Answer the question below the images.
